questions.question: Which band released the 1969 album 'Abbey Road'?
questions.explanation: Abbey Road was the Beatles' penultimate released album, named after the London studio where it was recorded.

questions.question: Which singer is known as the 'King of Pop'?
questions.explanation: Michael Jackson earned the nickname in the 1980s, after the success of the album 'Thriller'.

questions.question: Which composer wrote 'The Four Seasons', a set of four violin concertos?
questions.explanation: Vivaldi composed The Four Seasons around 1718–1720.

questions.question: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.explanation: A violin has four strings, tuned G, D, A and E.

questions.question: Which instrument has 88 keys on a standard full-size model?
questions.explanation: A standard modern piano has 52 white keys and 36 black keys.

questions.question: Which band released the 1973 album 'The Dark Side of the Moon'?
questions.explanation: Pink Floyd's album stayed on the Billboard 200 chart for hundreds of weeks.

questions.question: Which Swedish group won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with 'Waterloo'?
questions.explanation: ABBA's Eurovision win with 'Waterloo' launched their international career.

questions.question: Which rapper's real name is Marshall Mathers?
questions.explanation: Eminem takes his stage name from the initials M&M, for Marshall Mathers.

questions.question: Which singer is widely known as the 'Queen of Soul'?
questions.explanation: Aretha Franklin, who recorded 'Respect' in 1967, was given the title and was the first woman inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

questions.question: Which British band's line-up was Freddie Mercury, Brian May, Roger Taylor and John Deacon?
questions.explanation: Queen formed in London in 1970.

questions.question: In music, what does 'crescendo' mean?
questions.explanation: Crescendo means to gradually increase the volume. Its opposite is diminuendo.

questions.question: In music, what does the tempo marking 'adagio' indicate?
questions.explanation: Adagio means slow, at ease; it is slower than andante and faster than largo.

questions.question: Which composer wrote the opera 'The Magic Flute'?
questions.explanation: Mozart premiered The Magic Flute in Vienna in 1791, the year he died.

questions.question: Which South Korean group released the 2020 single 'Dynamite'?
questions.explanation: BTS's 'Dynamite' was their first single sung entirely in English.

questions.question: Which band released the 1977 album 'Rumours'?
questions.explanation: Rumours was recorded by Fleetwood Mac amid breakups within the band and became one of the best-selling albums ever.

questions.question: Which artist released the 2016 visual album 'Lemonade'?
questions.explanation: Beyoncé released Lemonade in April 2016, with a film aired on HBO.

questions.question: Which composer continued writing his Ninth Symphony even after becoming almost completely deaf?
questions.explanation: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony, completed in 1824, includes the 'Ode to Joy'.

questions.question: Who directed the 1975 thriller 'Jaws'?
questions.explanation: Jaws was directed by Steven Spielberg and is often credited as the first summer blockbuster.

questions.question: Which film won the Academy Award for Best Picture at the 2020 ceremony?
choices: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
questions.explanation: Parasite, by Bong Joon-ho, was the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture.

questions.question: Which actor played Forrest Gump in the 1994 film?
questions.explanation: Tom Hanks won his second consecutive Best Actor Oscar for the role.

questions.question: Who directed the 1994 film 'Pulp Fiction'?
questions.explanation: Pulp Fiction, directed by Quentin Tarantino, won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1994.

questions.question: Which actor played Jack Dawson in the 1997 film 'Titanic'?
questions.explanation: Leonardo DiCaprio starred opposite Kate Winslet in James Cameron's Titanic.

questions.question: Which Studio Ghibli film won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature in 2003?
questions.explanation: Hayao Miyazaki's Spirited Away won at the 2003 ceremony.

questions.question: Who directed the 2023 film 'Oppenheimer'?
questions.explanation: Christopher Nolan's Oppenheimer won seven Oscars, including Best Picture, at the 2024 ceremony.

questions.question: Which film franchise features characters wielding lightsabers?
questions.explanation: Lightsabers are the signature weapon of the Jedi and Sith in Star Wars.

questions.question: Which company created Mario?
questions.explanation: Mario was created by Shigeru Miyamoto and debuted at Nintendo in the arcade game Donkey Kong (1981).

questions.question: Which is the best-selling video game of all time?
questions.explanation: Minecraft has sold over 300 million copies, the most of any game, according to its publisher.

questions.question: In Tetris, what are the falling pieces called?
questions.explanation: Each piece is a tetromino, made of four connected squares.

questions.question: In which video game series do you play as Link in the kingdom of Hyrule?
questions.explanation: Link is the hero of The Legend of Zelda series. Zelda is the princess, not the player's character.

questions.question: In chess, which piece moves in an L-shape?
questions.explanation: The knight moves two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular, and it can jump over pieces.

questions.question: In which year was the arcade game Pac-Man first released?
questions.explanation: Namco released Pac-Man in Japan in 1980.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?
questions.explanation: Jane Austen published Pride and Prejudice in 1813.

questions.question: Who wrote the dystopian novel '1984'?
questions.explanation: George Orwell published Nineteen Eighty-Four in 1949.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel 'Don Quixote'?
questions.explanation: Cervantes published the first part of Don Quixote in 1605, often called the first modern novel.

questions.question: Which author created the detective Sherlock Holmes?
questions.explanation: Arthur Conan Doyle introduced Sherlock Holmes in 'A Study in Scarlet' (1887).

questions.question: Who wrote the novel 'One Hundred Years of Solitude'?
questions.explanation: Gabriel García Márquez published the novel in 1967. It helped define magical realism.

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted it in the early 1500s, and it hangs in the Louvre in Paris.

questions.question: Who painted 'The Starry Night'?
questions.explanation: Van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889 while staying in an asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence.

questions.question: Which artist painted 'Guernica' in 1937?
questions.explanation: Picasso painted Guernica in response to the bombing of the Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

questions.question: Which museum in Paris houses the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: The Louvre has displayed the Mona Lisa since 1797 and is the world's most visited art museum.
